exact_assets.description: Distressed circular emblem built around a Texas star in cream, dark navy/black, and brick red.
Outline of the real 130-plus-year-old original homestead house, used on product labels.
Printed product labels bearing the ranch mark; never invent packaging, ingredients, or product appearance.

facts.text: Every skincare product is made by the owners, Carol and Justin, by hand in their Texas kitchen, in small batches.
Tallow and lard products are made on the homestead, and many infusions are made in-house.
The brand's formulas are based on historical homestead recipes and traditions.
The ranch is named Rancho de Cinco Hijas, for the family's five daughters.
The outline of the ranch's 130-plus-year-old original homestead house appears on product labels.
The brand uses both tallow and lard, describing different functional roles for each rather than using tallow alone.
The brand avoids fragrance oils, using proprietary scent blends made from essential oils, and infuses some plants into carrier oils.
Cream products are unwhipped, not an air-entrained whipped formula, so the jar contains the full amount of product.
The catalog spans tallow soap bars, face and body creams, stick balms, and shave soaps, plus bundles.

visual_identity.logo_rules: Exact labels, the ranch emblem, and containers must remain real; generative images must never invent packaging, ingredients, or product appearance.
prohibited_visual_claims: sun rays or UV imagery implying tested sun protection
bug or insect imagery implying pest-repellent efficacy
ice pack, massage-on-injury, or joint/muscle-pain imagery implying pain relief
bandage, wound, or before/after skin-condition imagery implying treatment or healing
lab coat, syringe, or clinical imagery implying medical testing or endorsement
